messages.content:
Here is the trip. It is everything you get.

Shape: city-and-culture
Leaving from: Toronto
Going to: Rome
Dates: 2027-10-09 to 2027-10-16, fixed
Travellers: 2
Ages that change the plan: 68, 71
Access needs: One of us can walk a few kilometres a day but not on cobbles for long, and stairs without a handrail are difficult.
Budget: 350 CAD, per-day
Appetite for effort: gentle
Roughest night they will accept: hotel
Would rule the trip out: Nothing that needs to be at a place before 09:00, No guided group tours

About this city-and-culture:
Pace: slow
Interests: Roman archaeology, Baroque painting, markets
In their words: We have been to Rome once, thirty years ago, and saw the obvious things then. We would rather spend a whole morning in one place than see four.

candidates.title: Palazzo Altemps and Palazzo Massimo
candidates.summary: Two Roman National Museum sites with ancient sculpture, frescoes and mosaics in step-free-friendly galleries with lifts; a quiet way to see Roman archaeology indoors. Treat as two visits; I could not confirm current lift access in every wing or opening hours.

candidates.title: Galleria Borghese Baroque masterpieces
candidates.summary: Bernini sculpture and Caravaggio paintings in one villa, with timed entry in two-hour slots. The grounds are flat paths, though gravel may be tiring. Entry is by reservation, so booking lead time is unconfirmed; I could not check slot times against your no-before-09:00 rule.

candidates.title: Caravaggio paintings at San Luigi dei Francesi and Sant'Agostino
candidates.summary: Free church visits to see Caravaggio's works in their original settings, close together with short walking. Churches often close midday and floors can be uneven; I could not confirm current hours.

candidates.title: Galleria Doria Pamphilj
candidates.summary: A private palace gallery with Caravaggio, Velazquez and Titian, and an audio guide, so no group tour is needed. Rooms are on one main level, but I could not confirm lift or handrail details.

candidates.title: Baths of Caracalla
candidates.summary: Vast imperial bath ruins to explore at your own pace, a good fit for a slow morning on mostly level ground, though some surfaces are uneven. Opening hours and access paths were not confirmed.

candidates.title: Campo de' Fiori market morning
candidates.summary: A daily produce market with food stalls and a lively square. The square is cobbled, which may be tiring for one of you, so allow for sitting at a cafe. Market is typically in the morning; I could not verify current days.

candidates.title: Mercato Testaccio food market
candidates.summary: A covered, modern local market with a flat floor, good for lunch and browsing produce away from the tourist crowds. Hours and closed days were not confirmed.

candidates.title: Capitoline Museums
candidates.summary: Ancient Roman sculpture, the Capitoline Wolf and a Baroque picture gallery, linked by galleries with lifts. The piazza approach is cobbled but short. Could not confirm lift locations or hours.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel near Piazza Barberini / Via Veneto
candidatesAccepted.summary: A mid-range hotel in a flatter, smoother-paved area close to Baroque painting at Palazzo Barberini and a metro stop. Step-free entry, lift and handrails on stairs are not confirmed, so ask before booking. Rates for October 2027 were not checked and the budget of 350 CAD per day may not cover lodging and all other costs.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel near Piazza del Popolo
candidatesAccepted.summary: A hotel near the Popolo area, which has Caravaggio paintings in Santa Maria del Popolo and is largely level and walkable. Cobbles are nearby, so a taxi for short trips may help. Lift access and room accessibility were not verified, and neither was the price.
